referents.why: 'Never may it be' (Μὴ γένοιτο) is an optative with an impersonal subject; no candidate fits.
'It has been written' is a passive with no agent; the scripture is the subject. The builder's 'man' is wrong: it is not the one who wrote.
The quoted 'you' (second singular, may be justified) addresses God, the addressee of the psalm quoted; w5 is God.
The second quoted verb (will prevail) has the same second-person subject, God, as cl4.
'Of You' (σου) is the possessor of 'words'; the words are God's, so the referent is God.
The accusative 'you' (σε) is the subject of the infinitive 'being judged' in the quotation, and it is God.

links.why: The purpose sits in the quoted words, not in the citation frame 'it has been written'; the frame is the saying and gets a content link instead.
This is a Hebrew fronted כִּי link. Here ἐν τῷ + infinitive is a temporal ('when being judged'), which the within link carries.
links.category: Hebrew link used for Greek temporal

links.why: The second quoted verb falls under the same ὅπως as cl4, joined by καί; its purpose comes through cl4, not from the frame.
δέ after a rejection is a correction ('rather'), not a plain 'and'.
Two jussives, 'let God be true' and 'let every man be a liar' (verb elided), joined by δέ: one run of commands.
καί joins two subjunctives under one ὅπως: 'be justified and prevail'.
links.category: two verbs under one clause joined by and

links.why: The frame 'as it is written' (καθάπερ) is a comparison, not a plain 'and'; it is a separate sentence of citation.
A negative exclamation then δέ with a correcting jussive: 'Never may it be; rather let God be true'.
καθάπερ ('just as') compares the statement of 'every man a liar' with what is written; the compared clause is a saying.
The citation clause (it has been written) introduces what is quoted, so content links it to the quoted clause (R1).
ὅπως ('so that') gives the aim of God's being true: a third-person command followed by a second-person subjunctive, as the rule for a purpose after a command.
The infinitive phrase ἐν τῷ κρίνεσθαι σε sits in a prepositional role of cl5 (temporal 'when'); within carries that role.
links.category: temporal clause nested in verb phrase

groups.why: Only the two jussives joined by δέ form one imperative group; 'Never may it be' is a rejection formula, not a command, and 'part' is not a role of this kind.
The quoted psalm as a unit: the citation formula is its frame and the quoted words are its parts. No writer is named, so there is no sender.

none_fit.what: A rejection of the claim in 3:3; no link type records a disavowal of the preceding question.

none_fit.where: cl5 to cl6 (ἐν τῷ κρίνεσθαι, 'when being judged')
none_fit.what: A temporal 'when' clause has no link type of its own; recorded as within, with the temporal role stated in why.

cant_tell.what: the purpose reading of cl1 to cl4
cant_tell.why: Whether the quoted ὅπως clause states God's aim in being true, or only the psalm's own purpose, is a reading; I added the link because the form allows it, and it is open to review.
